gaps.sentence: She ___ have missed the train, or perhaps the car broke down — there is no way of knowing.
gaps.explanation: 'Might have missed' — possible but not certain.

gaps.sentence: How ___ you speak to me like that!
gaps.hint: outrage with the phrase how dare
gaps.explanation: 'How dare you' expresses outrage at someone's behavior: dare.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.
'Would you like …?' is the standard polite offer.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on, so they ___ be home.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses a confident conclusion from evidence.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.
